summary: Rule 71(3) communication of 2025-08-29. Four months end on 2025-12-29, inside the EPO closure, so the period ends on 2026-01-02 (OJ EPO 2025 A40). The grant fee was paid in time.
Rule 71(3) communication of 2025-08-29 with the same period end, 2026-01-02. No act; the loss of rights is effective 2026-01-03 and noted on 2026-01-21 (row 11).
A first Rule 71(3) communication (row 1), then a second one (row 2) after the register event GRAJ. The deadline of row 1 is superseded.
The same pattern on a second file: row 9, then row 10.

Rule 71(3) communication of 2026-04-01. Four months end on Saturday 2026-08-01, so the period ends on Monday 2026-08-03. No grant fee or loss of rights is in the FlowLeap data up to 2026-11-05: overdue at the clock 'fetch'.
German Article 94(3) communication of 2026-09-18 with its annex. The period is stated in the letter. A due date in 2027 needs the 2027 EPO closing days (OJ EPO 2026 A30).
English Article 94(3) communication of 2026-06-09 with its annex.
English Rule 71(3) communication of 2026-09-29 with the text intended for grant. Four months end on 2027-01-29, so the engine needs the 2027 closing days.

Communication of a notice of opposition (Rule 79(1) EPC) of 2026-10-14, with a period of four months for the proprietor. The opposition was filed on 2026-09-30, the last day of the nine months from the mention of grant on 2025-12-31.

Chosen case for the letter with two dates. EPA Form 2015C is dated 2026-01-21, and its body names the Rule 71(3) communication of 2025-08-29. The further-processing period runs from the notification of this letter, so a reader that takes the body date computes a wrong deadline. The form is not Form 2004C, so the office event is entered by hand (case S3b).

Second letter with two dates: dated 2026-10-14, with (06/10/26) in the form footer beside the form number. Every EPO form in this seed except rows 8 and 11 prints such a footer date, so nearly every letter has two dates.

Every document in this seed is a register copy with no text layer: pdffonts lists no font, and each page is a 300 dpi CCITT image. Row 2 is the chosen example. The applicant-side priority document (download row 12) is not in the package: the EPO letters cover the case (decision D3).
Two attorneys share a matter: jonas is responsible and lena is a co-attorney. Both may decide a code and confirm a deadline that the other proposed.
Handover from lena to anna with the instruction 'Check the text intended for grant of the Rule 71(3) communication of 29 September 2026'. anna sees the matter only from 2026-10-15.
Two readers agree on a Form 2004C letter, so the reading counts as checked (two-readers).
tobias enters the office event and the further-processing deadline by hand. The record refuses tobias as confirmer and refuses sabine (outside the wall); anna or the partner confirms.
The readers differ on the date of the letter with two dates. The person who decides the date cannot confirm the deadline.
The Article 94(3) Ticket is routed to jonas. lena and the partner see it and get not-routed-person when they try to decide.
A run for jonas whose Mandate names all WAGO matters reads EP21755382 and EP24166597, never EP22213933 (screen). The same run for the partner reads all three; a run for felix reads none.
